independent_review.text:
# Independent progress-bar default-token review

The bounded patch is supported for integration, subject to the integrator checking its base against the current tree and preserving unrelated concurrent changes. Reviewed patch SHA256 `cb824888aae78011e7274546d7e40ae1dbee0f899966bf3dfc73f85e18c82c8c`, qualification JSON SHA256 `340c628fd116e1626f5f38d73e37871f0461985edb8f9fa0e9019390884141e1`, base `0c25c56282d805aaed351b94a9729303462bfb2a`. No production template, stylesheet, public declaration text, or other component is changed.

The untouched Material 16.2.14 reference commit `df60e733c60e572ba538f6ad0ceff3e63e527b53` imports the current progress-bar default token into its legacy component and re-exports that same token under the legacy name. The patch restores that identity with the installed peer's exported `MAT_PROGRESS_BAR_DEFAULT_OPTIONS`; it intentionally changes DI so either public alias configures both generations, as in the reference. The minimum peer is 22.1.7: its package publicly exports `@angular/material/progress-bar`, whose declaration exports the token and structurally matching optional `color` and `mode` fields without a deprecation annotation on this token. Peer M3 color support has its own documented limitation; this review does not assert M3 styling behavior.

I independently checked the full 512 regular members of each retained tarball against its extracted package: no differences. Baseline SHA256 `1bd04f3629f84af7b34eaaa981c561f8415919866512e004e0e130bd01beb9bf`; candidate `48a20a314c30c9a2dcf659b680d9e91b73a935f5fb5f63955b284f3af0f72615`. Across packages only the progress-bar FESM, its source map and its declaration map differ; the FESM change is the new public peer import and alias in place of the independent token. All 45 `.d.ts` files are byte-identical. Both candidate source member hashes match the qualification.

The retained same-fixture ChromeHeadless baseline report SHA256 `fc7672634d830678d47a2115fbb9e75c73504d7ad89b4c1775ae4b2654cc1775` has 28/31 passing: identity, peer-token-to-legacy, and legacy-token-to-peer tests fail. Candidate report SHA256 `86c299060465510b4aa284bdd56af517da4578be0182d710698ba2cabe47d817` has 31/31, none skipped. The tests check both aliases in separate TestBed scopes, unrelated token isolation, legacy empty-option fallback and numeric value coercion. Reports identify extracted roots and have null artifact hashes; the independent tarball/member comparisons provide file identity but these are not sealed `--run` reports. Candidate pack predates final test-only description labels, with production source unchanged.

This is a focused review of retained evidence; no independent browser rerun was performed. It does not grant zoneless, full artifact suite, browser matrix, 21.x, security or release qualification. Any related authored-use source epoch must be independently updated where applicable rather than treated as automatically qualified by this change.
